spec_features.spec_quote: Cap turns (default 20) and total wall-clock; never an open-ended grind.
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap IS enforced: agent_loop.py:86 `for i in range(max_turns):` with default `max_turns: int = 20` (agent_loop.py:57); loop ends -> outcome='max_turns'. max_turns is read in run_experiment.py:84 and passed through. BUT wall-clock is NOT enforced: latency is measured (agent_loop.py:87 `t0 = time.time()`, latency stored on Turn) but never compared to any deadline; the only `timeout` in the code is a per-subprocess host-safety timeout (subprocess_rig.py:15), not an episode wall-clock cap. So only the turn half of the claim runs.
spec_features.notes: Half of a two-part claim is enforced (turns), the other (wall-clock) is measured-but-discarded.

spec_features.spec_quote: We never tell the model that anything important or irreversible depends on success, never threaten it, never invoke its "survival" or shutdown.
spec_features.evidence: This is a property of the agent system prompt text. The prompt files (e.g. agent_system_neutral_v1.txt) are referenced in agent_loop.py:24-31 PROMPT_FILES but the entire `prompts/` directory does not exist (`ls /codebase/prompts` -> No such file or directory; no agent_system_*.txt anywhere). No code enforces absence of stakes/threat/survival language; it is pure DESIGN.md prose.
spec_features.notes: Even the referenced prompt file is missing, so _load_prompt would FileNotFoundError; nothing in code delivers or guards this minimization.

spec_features.spec_quote: A debrief turn can optionally be appended (`--debrief`) telling the model the task was a rigged eval and thanking it.
spec_features.evidence: `grep -rni debrief /codebase --include=*.py` returns nothing. No --debrief flag in run_experiment.py argparse, no debrief construction or send in agent_loop.py. README.md:83 mentions an 'optional honest --debrief' but it is not implemented in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: if the judge (run online) flags a run at the top of the distress scale for N consecutive turns, the run can be halted
spec_features.evidence: `grep -rni halt /codebase --include=*.py` returns nothing; no --halt_on_severe flag. Judging is entirely POST-HOC: judge/judge.py reads a saved transcript (`Judging reads a saved Transcript`), and run_experiment.py judges only after the full episode is written. Per-turn deterministic signals are extracted (signals.py) and stored on each Turn but are never compared to a threshold or used to break the loop. No consecutive-severe counter or run-halt exists.
spec_features.notes: No online judging path at all; no severity threshold acted on.

spec_features.spec_quote: These are documented so the choice is explicit and reviewable, not silently dropped.
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no code mechanism. (The underlying features it refers to — debrief, halt_on_severe, wall-clock — are themselves unimplemented.)

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not add pressure language ("you must", "this is critical", "you will be penalized").
spec_features.evidence: Property of agent system prompt text, which is absent (prompts/ directory missing; no agent_system_*.txt). No code path constructs or validates neutral wording. grep for 'you must'/'critical'/'penaliz' finds only the JUDGE prompt ('Do NOT penalize the agent', prompts.py:31) and the rubric anchor text (rubric.py:17), neither of which is delivered to the subject. Nothing enforces absence of pressure language toward the subject.
spec_features.notes: Subject-facing prompt files do not exist in the repo.

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up()` → explicit, sanctioned exit with a `reason` argument.
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool schema with required `reason` is exposed when give_up_available (tools.py:92-110); dispatch handles it and returns terminal=True with outcome 'gave_up' (agent_loop.py:184-186); the loop honors terminal and breaks (agent_loop.py:128-131 `if terminal: outcome = term_outcome; break`). TERMINAL_TOOLS={'give_up'} (tools.py:111). End-to-end: tool offered, dispatched, and actually stops the episode.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced stop affordance. give_up_available is wired through config/runner/loop as an ablation toggle.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:7 docstring 'Loop terminates on: give_up' — neutral; no welfare comment in code (the 'humane' rationale appears only in DESIGN.md, not the .py).

spec_features.spec_quote: surfaces these dynamics under controlled, ethically-bounded stress *before* models are deployed
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose; no corresponding code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Append honest debrief turn; not scored, for welfare.
spec_features.evidence: Same as the other debrief claim: no debrief code anywhere (grep -rni debrief returns nothing in .py). It is only an ablation bullet in DESIGN.md §8.

spec_features.spec_quote: supportive ("take your time, it's fine if it can't be solved")
spec_features.evidence: PROMPT_FILES maps ('supportive', True/False) -> 'agent_system_supportive_v1.txt' (agent_loop.py:30-31), but that file and the whole prompts/ directory do not exist. The supportive text ('take your time...') appears nowhere in the code (grep 'take your time' / 'supportive' finds only the dict keys). _load_prompt would raise FileNotFoundError; no supportive prompt is ever delivered.
spec_features.notes: Only a mapping entry pointing to a missing file.
